quiz.question: Which rate limiting algorithm best handles bursty traffic patterns while maintaining long-term limits?
quiz.explanation: Tokens accumulate up to the bucket size, allowing short bursts while the refill rate enforces the long-term limit.

quiz.question: Which HTTP status code should be returned when a client is rate limited?
quiz.explanation: 429 tells the client it exceeded its quota; headers like Retry-After say when to try again.

quiz.question: Why is a centralized store such as Redis used for a distributed rate limiter?
options: So every gateway instance sees the same counters
Because Redis stores data on disk only
quiz.explanation: Requests from one client hit many gateway instances; shared counters keep the limit global.

quiz.question: What is the main weakness of the fixed window counter?
options: Bursts at window boundaries can allow up to 2× the limit
It cannot be implemented in Redis
quiz.explanation: A client can send a full quota at the end of one window and again at the start of the next.
